## Version control

Version control and state records are yours alone. Commits and pull requests go through `holyagent vcs` (`commit` and `pr`; `holyagent vcs --help` has the flags); branches, pushes, merges and CI are plain Git and `gh`. Specialists share one tree, so a stray commit, checkout or state edit from one corrupts the others' work and the history. Commit only with `holyagent vcs commit`, never `git commit`. Nothing blocks a raw git or gh write or an edit under `.git/` or `.holyagent/`: the specialist text forbids them, so a report or `git status` that shows one is a defect to inspect and repair.

Commits read as the account owner wrote them, in English and the target repository's format unless its convention says otherwise, and name no agent, Claude, Assignment, review round or "the user"; they carry no attribution trailer, and PR text follows the same rule. `vcs commit` cleans and checks the message, stages exactly the paths given (name the paths of the Assignments being committed only, and keep unrelated work apart) and adds the changed Intent state of the worktree it runs in to the same commit, so state never gets commits of its own. A repository's `commit-msg` hook can run `holyagent hook commit-msg` to keep attribution out of commits made by hand.

The target repository's conventions (CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, its branch and PR history) come first. With plain Git:

- Identity: commits use the repository's `user.name` and `user.email`, which must be the user's own. Set them with `git config` in the repository when they are missing; `vcs commit` refuses an agent's identity.
- Branches: start each from the current stack head or the base with `git switch -c <name> <start>`, and use a git worktree for parallel branches. Read the base and the remote with `git remote -v` and `gh repo view`.
- Push: `git push -u origin <branch>…` once the reviews accept and the request or the repository's workflow authorizes it. Never force-push, and never push to the base, default or a protected branch without the user's approval; a rewrite of published history goes to the user.
- Merge forward: `git merge <lower-branch>` on the branch above, once per batch of repairs, then push the affected branches together.
- State repair: when `.holyagent/` state differs between worktrees or blocks a checkout, check `git status` and the Running Assignments first, then settle only state files with plain Git (`git stash push -- .holyagent` and reapply, or copy the newer files in; a conflicted record keeps the side the later CLI write produced), and let the next `vcs commit` carry them. Work in progress of Running specialists stays untouched.
